title: Crypto Phishing: 3 Fake Message Tricks Every Beginner Should Spot
caption: Educational only. Not financial advice. Phishing uses fake messages and links to trick people into giving up access. Sources: FTC, Investopedia. AI-generated voice. Educational only. Not financial advice.

scenes.head: A MESSAGE ARRIVES
scenes.narration: A message says your crypto account has a problem. Click this link now. Is it real, or is it a trap?

scenes.head: THIS IS PHISHING
scenes.narration: It is called phishing. Scammers pretend to be a trusted company, using fake emails, fake websites, and fake support chats.

scenes.head: TRICK ONE: URGENCY
scenes.narration: Trick one is urgency. Messages say act now or lose your account. Pressure is meant to stop you from thinking.

scenes.head: TRICK TWO: LOOKALIKES
scenes.narration: Trick two is lookalike links. A web address may have a small spelling change that is easy to miss.

scenes.head: TRICK THREE: SECRETS
scenes.narration: Trick three is asking for secrets. Real services never need your seed phrase or password sent in a message.

scenes.head: STAY SAFE
scenes.narration: Type the website address yourself, never share your seed phrase, and turn on two factor login.
